name: Summer Engineering Awareness Program
what_you_do: A free summer program for rising juniors and seniors. You hear lectures and do lab work and group projects. You try six kinds of engineering. They are civil, chemical, electrical, computer, environmental and mechanical. You learn how to apply to college.
grades: Students currently in 10th or 11th grade (rising juniors and seniors)
who_can_apply: Students now enrolled in 10th or 11th grade. The page says selection is based in part on strong math and science skills and interest in engineering.
pay_detail: Free to participants. Corporate and individual sponsors pay for it. You get a certificate and an application fee waiver at Manhattan University.
duration: Choose a 6-day or 10-day session. The page lists 2027 dates: June 25-26 and June 28 to July 1 (8 AM to 3 PM); July 7-9, 12-16 and 19-20 (10-day program, 8:30 AM to 3 PM); and July 22-23 and 26-29.
deadline_text: No application deadline is posted on the page. The listed session dates are for 2027.
how_to_apply: The page gives no application form. It says to complete the registration form, and the page lists the program director, Dr. Walter P. Saukin, at 718-862-7171 (Monday to Friday, 9:30 AM to 4 PM). Call to ask how to apply.
notes: The school is now called Manhattan University, formerly Manhattan College. The page says the program has run for over 40 years. The page lists a free program. It comes with a certificate and no fee to apply at Manhattan University. The page lists an email for the director that does not match the director's name, so call instead. Confirm the steps with the director.
